question: Were any of the tests covering your change skipped? Answer yes or no, then explain.
answer:
Yes. Three tests in `tests/test_redis_cache.py` were skipped in every run because no Redis server is available here. One of them, `test_get_or_compute_caches_falsy_value`, is the existing test written specifically for fix #1 (falsy values being recomputed). The other two, `test_get_or_compute_caches_value` and `test_ttl_is_applied`, also exercise `RedisCache`, the class I changed.

Only fix #1 was affected; the tests for fixes #2 and #3 ran and passed. For fix #1, I added 6 test cases that use an in-memory stand-in for the Redis client. They ran and passed. I also checked that all 6 fail when the old code is put back, so they do catch the bug.

What hasn't been tested is the fix running against a real Redis server. My stand-in only imitates the client's `get`, `set` and `delete`. It returns bytes, as the real client does by default, but it is not the real client. That's why I set `verified_by_tests` to true and also listed the skipped tests in `side_effects`. To close the gap, run `pytest` with `KVCACHE_REDIS_URL` pointing at a Redis instance before release.
